title: Symbols and editing in place
summary: Turn a drawing into a graphic symbol, place it twice, edit it in place and watch both copies change, then tint one and set how a graphic loops.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
In this lesson you will turn this plain face into a symbol, put two of it on the stage, and give both a face by drawing on just one of them.

A symbol is drawn once and kept in the Library; each copy on the stage is an instance of it. Change the symbol and every instance changes.

steps.title: Pick the Selection tool
steps.text: Press V, or click the arrow at the top of the toolbox.

steps.title: Select the face
steps.text: Double-click the yellow face to select its fill and its outline together.

steps.title: Convert it to a symbol
steps.text:
Press F8, or choose Modify > Convert to Symbol. Name it Face, set Type to Graphic, and click OK.

The face is now an instance, shown with a box around it when selected.

steps.title: Place a second face
steps.text:
Face is now in the Library. Drag it from the Library onto the right side of the stage to place a second instance.

You can also press Ctrl+D (Edit > Duplicate) with the face selected, drag the copy to the right, and click Next.

steps.title: Edit in place
steps.text: Double-click the face on the left. You are now inside the symbol: the rest of the stage is dimmed, and the edit bar above the stage reads Scene 1 › Face.

steps.title: Pick the Oval tool
steps.text: Press O, and choose a dark fill color with the fill swatch at the bottom of the toolbox.

steps.title: Draw an eye
steps.text: Draw a small oval for the left eye.

steps.title: And another
steps.text: Draw the right eye. Watch the other face as you let go.

steps.title: Both faces changed
steps.text:
The face on the right has eyes too, though you never touched it. Both instances show the same symbol, so editing it once changes them all.

Add a mouth if you like, then click Next.

steps.title: Back to the scene
steps.text: Press V for the Selection tool, then double-click an empty part of the stage. You can also click Scene 1 at the left of the edit bar, or press Ctrl+E.

steps.title: Select one face
steps.text: Click the face on the right. A single click selects the whole instance; its settings show on the Properties panel's Object tab.

steps.title: Tint it
steps.text:
Under Color Effect, open the Style list and choose Tint.

A color effect belongs to the instance, not the symbol, so only this face changes.

steps.title: Choose the tint
steps.text: Click the Tint swatch to pick the color, and drag the percentage beside it to set how strongly it is applied. Red, Green and Blue set the color by numbers.

steps.title: Looping
steps.text:
A graphic symbol's timeline plays in step with the timeline it sits on. The Looping options say how: Loop repeats it, Play Once stops at its end, and Single Frame holds one frame, set by First. Reverse and ping-pong options play it backward.

Choose Single Frame now. With one frame in Face it looks the same, but on a symbol of mouth shapes or poses, this is how you pick the one to show.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You made a graphic symbol, placed it twice, edited it in place to change both instances, tinted one, and set how it loops.

Save with Ctrl+S if you want to keep it. Help > Tutorials has more lessons; if you have not animated a symbol yet, try Your first animation.
